gdesc.Actinomycetes|Actinomyces: Actinomyces are Gram-positive, rod shaped, irregularly staining bacteria that resembles fungi in appearance because they form filamentous growth. They are non-sporeforming, non- acid fast and non motile. Most species preferentially grows in the absence of oxygen but some species can grow well under its presence also. Whether pathogenic or non-pathogenic, they form a major component of oral microflora .The production of antibiotic by Actinomyces, such as Streptomyces griseus is extremely important in the pharmaceutical industry. Other Actinomyces are human pathogens. They ferments carbohydrates with production of acid but no gas. Some species may show greening or complete lysis of rabbit red blood cells.This genus consist of 37 species. Some important members of this genus are A.israelli , A.bovis and A. canis.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acetobacter: The members of this genus are Gram-negative, ellipsoidal to rod shaped bacteria. They grow in the presence of oxygen. Acetobacter show motility by peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the cell). Fruits, as source of sugar and of ethanol, are excellent habitat for acetic acid bacteria. Acetic acid bacteria have been found on various fruits such as apples, apricot, almonds, beets, bananas, oranges, pineapples etc. They are also found in various beverages such as beer, wine, vinegar and soft drinks. The acetic acid bacteria have been used since historic times for vinegar productions by converting ethanol to acetic acid. The important members of this genus areAcetobacter acetiand Acetobacter liquefaciens This genus comprises of 32 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acholeplasma: Acholeplasma are Gram-negative bacteria. Their shape varies from spherical or pear-shaped structures to branched or helical filaments. Acholeplasma are facultative anaerobes i.e., they can grow both in the presence as well in the absence of oxygen. Acholeplasma are parasites of humans, animals, arthropods and plants. Acholeplasma species can be found in the gut contents of a wide range of host insects. Its important members are Acholeplasma axanthum , Acholeplasma brassicae and Acholeplasma oculi .17 species comprises this genus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Achromobacter: Members of this genus are Gram-negative rods or cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria). They grow slowly in the presence of oxygen. Achromobacter are widespread in soil and water; and are plant growth promoters. This genus consists of 7 species. Its important members are A.denitrificans and A.spanius.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acidianus: The members of Acidianus are Gram-negative cocci. They are usually strict anaerobes (i.e., they live in the absence of oxygen) but may be aerobic or facultative. Acidianus sp. are widespread and can be isolated exclusively from continental solfatara fields, where they thrive within hot, highly acidic water and mudholes. Acidic pH, absence or limitation of organic substrates, and elevated temperature favours growth of Acidianus. By means of sulfide oxidation, several isolates of Acidianus are able to extract metal ions from sulfide ores (“bioleaching”). This genus comprises of only three species , viz., Acidianus infernos, Acidianus brierleyi and Acidianus ambivalens.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acidiphilium: This genus comprises of Gram-negative, rod shaped, acidophilic bacteria (organisms that has its optimum growth in acidic pH).They grow well in the presence of oxygen. They are found commonly in acidic mineral environment. Only 8 species have been reported in this genus .Some important members of this genus are Acidiphilium cryptum , Acidiphilium rubrum and Acidiphilium acidophilum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acidovorax: Acidovorax species are Gram-negative rods. They exhibit motility by means of single polar flagella. They constitute a group of aerobic organism growing well in a variety of organic acids and amino acids. Most of these organisms are of clinical origin and a minority is from soil. The important members of this genus are Acidovorax facilis, Acidovorax temperans and Acidovorax avenae. This genus comprises of 10 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Acinetobacter: The genus Acinetobacter includes Gram–negative saprophytes (organisms that usually grows on decomposing organic matter). They have short, plump rod-shaped structures. They are ubiquitous organisms that are present in soil, water and sewage. Member of the genus are also found in variety of foodstuffs, including milk products and fresh meat. They are the normal inhabitant of human skin and have been particularly associated with moist skin areas such as toe webs, the groins and axilla. Their pathogenesis is generally low but they may cause occasional serious opportunistic infections including meningitis, septicemia and pneumonia. There are 17 species present in this genus and some important one are Acinetobacter calcoaceticus, Acinetobacter haemolyticus and Acinetobacter johnsonii .
gdesc.Bacteria|Actinomadura: The members of Actinomudura are gram-positive actinomycetes which produce a branched substrate mycelium bearing aerial hyphae that undergoes differention into single or short chains of arthrospores. They are widely distributed in soil where they probably have a role in the turnover of organic matter. In humans, A.madurae and A.pelletieri cause mycetoma , a chronic disease of subcutaneous tissues and bones that is characterized by swelling ,abscesses and discharge of pus.Actinomudura strains are the source of new antibiotics, enzymes and products with pharmacological activity. Actinomadura madurae, Actinomadura fibrosa and Actinomadura citrea are some of its important members.This genus consist of 57 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Actinoplanes: Actinoplanes are Gram-positive actinomycetes that form non fragmenting branching mycelium ( a mass of branching tubular filament) with aerial growth. They form motile spores with polar flagella and grow only in the presences of oxygen. They are widely distributed in soil and decaying animal and plant material. Many of its members produce useful enzymes and secondary metabolite, so they may have important applications in industry, biotechnology and agriculture. This genus comprises of 25 species. . Its important members are Actinoplanes philippinensis, Actinoplanes regularis and Actinoplanes cyaneus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Aerococcus: Members of this genus are Gram-positivc cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria). They require a very low concentration of oxygen for their growth. Aerococci can be isolated from the air in hospital environments, from vegetation, outdoor air and dust; from human clinical specimens and as a marine organism causing a fatal disease of lobsters. Aerococci are the causative agent of different diseases such as osteomyelitis, endocarditis and septic arthritis. This genus comprises of only 5 species viz., A. viridans , A. urinaehominis , A. urinae , A. sanguinicola and A. christensenii.
gdesc.Bacteria|Aeromonas: Members of this genus are Gram-negative rods. They usually have a single polar flagellum, which imparts them motility. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Strains of Aeromonas have been isolated from a wide variety of water samples. Motile strains of Aeromonas causes human extra-intestinal infections, meningitis and bacteremia. A.hydrophila , one of the important member of this genus, causes disease in fish, frogs and several other animals. Some of its other important members are Aeromonas hydrophila ,Aeromonas salmonicida and Aeromonas veroniiv. This genus comprises of 19 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Agrobacterium: The genus comprises of single cell, Gram-negative, non- sporeforming rods. Agrobacterium possess few peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Most strains of Agrobacterum are plant pathogens and their natural habitat is on and around the roots and underground stem of some susceptible plants. Crown gall is an important economic disease caused by an agroabcterium i.e.,Agrobacterum tumefaciens. Its important members includes A.tumefaciens, A. radiobacter and A.atlanticum. This genus comprises of 11 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Agromyces: Agromyces are gram-positive, irregularly rod shaped bacteria, which are composed of branched, filamentous elements which ,as growth progresses, undergo septation and fragmentation to yield irregular forms. Agromyces require the presence of oxygen for its growth. The natural habitat of Agromyces is soil ranging from fertile meadow to barren soil. They are pathogenic to plants. Its important members includes A. ramosusv , A. rhizospherae and A.fucosus . This genus comprises of 11 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Alcaligenes: Alcaligenes are Gram- negative bacteria and their shape may range from coccus to rods. They are motile by peritrichous flagella. Alcaligenes grows strictly in the presence of oxygen. They seem to be ubiquitous and are widespread in soil, water, hospial environment and human clinical materials. Strains assigned to the genus Alcaligenes have been studied for the production of unnatural amino acids for possible applications in pharmaceutical industry. Members of this genus are opportunistic pathogens. some species like Alcaligenes faecalis may cause respiratory tract infection of birds. This genus consist of 16 species and some of its important members are A.faecalis, A. piechaudii and A. xylosoxidans.
gdesc.Bacteria|Alteromonas: The members of Alteromonas are Gram-negative, straight, curved or spiral rods. They are motile by means of polar flagella. Oxygen is required for their growth. Its members have a wide distribution throughout the coastal environment and open oceans. They have been found in varied biotypes; surface of biological or nonbiological submerged material; seawater sediments and guts of marine animals. Alteromonas putrefaciens contaminate numerous natural products and causes the putrefaction of preserved and fresh food. Its important members are Alteromonas macleodii , Alteromonas nigrifaciens and Alteromonas citrea.This genus comprises of 22 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Alysiella: Alysiella are Gram-positive, multicellular filamentous bacteria. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. They appear to be the residents of the healthy, normal oral cavities of warm blooded vertebrates. Only one species comprises this genus i.e., Alysiella filiformis.
gdesc.Bacteria|Anabaena:
This member of cyanobacteria (blue green algae ) are very commonly found in rice field.They fix nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts. They are beneficial because they contribute nitrogen in the soil.In most cases identification upto species level is not easy. 
There are Sixty records of this genus in this databse reported from...........
gdesc.Bacteria|Aquaspirillum: Aquaspirillum are helical shaped bacteria but can also be vibroid (A.delicatum) or straight rods (A.fasciculus). Members of this genus have flagella either at one or both ends. Aquaspirillum are typically aerobic but some are microaerophilic i.e., their growth is better in less oxygen concentration. Aquaspirillum generally thrives on various freshwater sources, including distilled water, ditch and canal water and sewage. This genus consists of 19 species. Some of its important members are Aquaspirillum serpens, Aquaspirillum psychrophilum and Aquaspirillum aquaticum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Arthrobacter: The members of this genus exhibit both rod and coccoid forms and stains Gram-positive They are usually non motile and grow in the absence of oxygen. Member of the genus Artrobacter form a numerically important fraction of the indigenous bacterial flora of soils. They have also been isolated from sewage and other similar habitat.They are also important agent of mineralization in soil and possibly also some other habitats. Among the compounds reported to be degraded by Arthrobacter are certain herbicides and pesticides. Some of its important members are Arthrobacter globiformis , Arthrobacter flavescens and Arthrobacter citreus. This genus comprises of 22 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Azomonas: The representatives of this genus are Gram – negative to Gram-variable (rarely) with ovoid, ellipsoidal or coccoid cells. They exhibit motility by means of a special type of flagellation. They grow well in the presence of oxygen. Members of this genus are primarily aquatic and since so far they have only been isolated from fresh water habitat.This genus comprises of only 3 species species viz., Azomonas agilis, Azomonas insignis and Azomonas macrocytogenes.
gdesc.Bacteria|Azotobacter: Azotobacter comprises of Gram-negative pleomorphic bacteria , the shape of which varies from blunt rods, oval to coccus shaped bacteria. They show motility by means of peritichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the cell). They grow in the presence of oxygen. Representatives of this genus are regular inhabitants of soil,fresh water bodies and plant surfaces such as the external environment of roots(rhizosphere) and leaves(phylosphere). Some species occur in marine habitat also. This genus comprises of nine species and some of its important members are Azotobacter chroococcum , Azotobacter beijerinckii and Azotobacter nigricans .
gdesc.Bacteria|Bacillus: Bacillus are rod shaped, motile bacteria. They are Gram-positive or positive only in the early stages of growth. Some members are strictly aerobic (oxygen requiring) while others may be anaerobes. They form heat resistant endospores. Bacillus popilliae and B.lentimorbes are defined in nature as obligate pathogens. They are found only in association with a specific insect disease or in surrounding soil in the spore state. Of the 183 species of the genus Bacillus, the two of the greatest medical important are B.anthracis ,the causative agent of anthrax, and B.cerus , which causes food poisoning.
gdesc.Bacteria|Bacteroides: Bacteroides are nonsporforming, Gram- negative rod shaped bacteria.They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. Members of the genus Bacteroides and related taxa normally colonize the upper respiratory tracts.these organisms are considered as the normal commmensal flora of the mucous membranes of human and animals. They have been found to be associated with dental plaque, intra-abdominal infection, perirectal abscesses and decubitus ulcers in human beings. This genus consist of 60 species and some of its important members include Bacteroides fragilis, Bacteroides coagulans and Bacteroides pyogenes.
gdesc.Bacteria|Beijerinckia: Members of this genus are Gram- negative, rod shaped bacterial cells with round ends containing polar lipoid bodies. Beijerinckia species are motile by peitrichous flagella with the exception of some strains of B.indica. They grow in the presence of the oxygen. They are found primarily in acid soils and can also be isolated from neutral and slightly alkaline tropical soils. B. tends to occur in large members in the rhizosphere of rice plants. This genus comprises of only 6 species. Few of its members are Beijerinckia indica, Beijerinckia derxii and Beijerinckia mobilis .
gdesc.Bacteria|Bordetella: The members of this genus are coccobacillus (very short rod shaped bacteria that looks roughly spherical). They grow in the presence of oxygen. Its members are usually isolated only during disease by nasal or tracheal swabbing from the respiratory tract of their primary host. All the members of the genus Bordetella are pathogens for example B. pertussis causes human whooping cough ; B.parapertussis causes a milder form of whooping cough in humans,and has recently been shown to cause chronic, non progressive pneumonia in lambs. Its important members are Bordetella pertussis , Bordetella trematum and Bordetella avium .
gdesc.Bacteria|Bradyrhizobium: Bradirhizobium are Gram-negative rods that are capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen. They require oxygen for their growth and grow slowly in comparison to other rhizobia on a particular media. They form complex symbiotic (mutually beneficial) relationship with leguminous plants such as cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). This genus comprises of four species viz., B.japonicum, B. liaoningense, B. yuanmingense and B. elkanii.
gdesc.Bacteria|Branhamella: The members of this genus are gram-negative small cocci, usually occurring in pairs with flattened adjacent side. Their optimum growth take place in the presence of oxygen at a temperature of 33-35°C. except B.catarhalis which is a well documented commensal (an organism living on or within another organism without injuring or benefiting the other organism)} and pathogen of human, other species have been found in association with guinea pigs, sheeps and rabbits respectively. Only one species comprises this genus and i.e., B.catarrhalis .
gdesc.Bacteria|Brevibacterium: Members of this genus are gram-positive. Cells from older cultures (3-7 days) are composed of roughly spherical cells, whereas irregular slender rods are characteristic of rapidly growing cells. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. Brevibacterium exist in a number of different habitats and especially in those having a high salt concentration. B.lines is a major component of the micro flora of surface ripened cheese. B.casei has been isolated from raw milk ,cheese, curd and cheddar cheese. Some of its important members are B. linens, B. iodinum, B.fermentans and B. epidermidis . This genus comprises of 29 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Brochothrix: The genus Brochothrix contains Gram-positive, non -sporeforming, rod-shaped bacteria that show characteristic changes in cell morphology during growth. They grow in the presence of oxygen. The natural habitat of Brochothrix sp. is not known with certainty. More recently Brochothrix thermosphacta has been isolated from a variety of source that include fish and fish products, frozen foods, milk, and cream. This genus comprises of only two species viz., B. thermosphacta and B. campestris .
gdesc.Bacteria|Brucella: Brucella are gram-negative coccobacilli (very short rod shaped bacteria that looks roughly spherical) or short chains or groups. Growth occurs in the presence of oxygen. Domestic animals are the primary reservoirs for Brucella and therefore constitute the major threat to human health. Members of this genus are facultative intracellular pathogens, which causes infectious disease of the genitourinary tract of sheep goats, pigs, cattle dogs, and other animals, and of the reticulo-endothelial system of humans. This genus consists of only six species. B. melitensis , B. suis , B. ovis , B. neotomae , B.canis and B. abortus .
gdesc.Bacteria|Butyrivibrio: Members of this genus are curved rods, and usually stains Gram-negative. These organisms show translational motility. They grow in the presence of oxygen. The members are the common inhabitants of the bovine rumen and are present in the gastrointestinal tract of variety of animals and have also been found in fecal materials of rabbits, horses and humans. Only three species are known to be present in this genus viz., B. fibrisolvens , B. crossotus and B. hungatei
gdesc.Bacteria|Campylobacter: All the members in the genus are slender, helically curved gram-negative rods. They are motile by means of a long single polar flagellum found at one or both ends of the cell. They require a very long level of oxygen for its optimum growth. Its distribution varies from the intestines of healthy pigs, cattle, sheep and human beings to genital organs of humans. They have also been isolated from human clinical samples. The genus Campylobacter contains both non-pathogenic and pathogenic species to humans and other animals. It is associated with variety of conditions in humans ranging from septicemia (presence of toxins and pathogens in the blood) to enteritis (inflammation of the intestinal tract). This genus consists of 25 species and some of its important members are C. fetus, C.coli , C.pylori and C.rectus .
gdesc.Bacteria|Caulobacter: The members of this genus are Gram-negative and give rise to two dissimilar cells, that are morphologically and behaviorally different after reproduction. They grow in the presence of oxygen. Practically any type of seawater from harbors, estuaries, the open ocean, deepsea , hydrothermal vents, storage reservoirs-contain Caulobacter. Caulobacterhave been demonstrated to be capable of rapidly mineralizing agricultural pollutants. This genus comprises of 17 species of which some important one are Caulobacter vibrioides, Caulobacter bacteroides and Caulobacter crescentus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Cellulomonas: They are Gram-positive, slender, irregular rods which may vary considerably in length and which may be arranged in V-formation. The main habitat of Cellulomonads appears to be the soil, but has also been found from rumen, activated sludge and cellulose enriched environments such as bark and wood and sugar fields. Like other cellulose and hemicellulose degrading organisms, Cellulomonas strains have been considered potential candidates for waste disposal. Cellulomonas consist of 15 species. Some of its important members are Cellulomonas flavigena , Cellulomonas fermentans and Cellulomonas persica .
gdesc.Bacteria|Chromobacterium: The genus Chromobacterium consist of Gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria with rounded ends. Members of this genus are usually motile by means of a single polar flagellum and by one to four lateral flagella. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Chromobacterium are found mainly in soil and water but have also been found associated with infections of humans and animals. This genus consists of only two species C.fluriatile and C.violaccum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Citrobacter: The members of this genus are gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria. They show motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Citrobacter are reported to occur in environments such as water, sewage, and soil. They have also been found as an intestinal commensal in humans. Some of its important members are Citrobacter freundii , Citrobacter diversus and Citrobacter rodentium. This genus consists of 12 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Clostridium: Clostridium, are Gram-positive rods. They are usually non-motile by means of flagella distributed over its surface (peritrichous flagella). They form endospores i.e., extremely heat and chemical resistant, thick wall spores that develops within bacteria. Due to the ubiquitous distribution of the clostridial spores and their resistance, the clostridia are present everywhere. Numbers of Clostridias are pathogens that produce toxins which can necrotiz body tissues or interfere with nerve transmission.The genus comprises of 189 species and some of its important members are Clostridium histolyticum, Clostridium putrefaciens and Clostridium tetani
gdesc.Bacteria|Comamonas: Comamonas cells are straight to slightly curved rods. They stains gram negative. A bipolar tuft of flagella is found in Comamonas . Comamonas strains have been isolated from soil, mud, water from natural and industrial environments and some strains from clinical samples. Comamonas strains may contribute to the natural biodegradation of various complex chemicals such as unsaturated carboxylic acid, aromatic acids, sterols and aromatic polymers of lignin type. This genus consist of 8 species out of which some of the important members are Comamonas terrigena , Comamonas denitrificansand Comamonas acidovorans
gdesc.Bacteria|Corynebacterium: Corynebacterium are Gram-positive bacteria, nevertheless some species (e.g., C.diptheriae) decolorize easily. Although some species are straight to slightly curved rods with irregularly stained segments and sometime granules. They frequently show club shaped swelling. Generally they are non-motile and can grow in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They are found in broad variety of habitat including soil, feces, dairy products, animal skins and plant materials. Corynebacterium occur either as true pathogens or as cutaneous or muco-cutaneous contaminants. This genus comprises of 112 species and some important Corynebacterium are C. diphtheriae, C. fascians, C. nigricans C.pyogenes and C.afermentans.
gdesc.Bacteria|Cytophaga: The members of Cytophaga are Gram-negative bacteria with rod shaped cells, which may differ substantially in shape. They may be short or long, delicate or stout, with tapering or rounded ends. Members of this genus can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They are found in enormous numbers in certain habitat, mainly those rich in organic material such as decaying plant material and dung of animals, particularly that of herbivorous. In fresh water environments, they are found on riverbanks and lakeshores, in estuaries, aerobic bottom sediments. Its important members are Cytophaga hutchinsonii , Cytophaga fermentans and Cytophaga flevensis .
gdesc.Bacteria|Derxia: They are gram-negative rods and cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria).Cells are motile by means of a short polar flagellum. They grow in the presence of oxygen. Derxia is primarily a soil organism occurring in tropical soils. The only known species in this genus is Derxia gummosa .
gdesc.Bacteria|Desulfomonas: The members of Desulfuromonas are gram negative, straight or slightly curved or ovoid rods. They are motile due to lateral or subpolar flagella. Their growth takes place in the absence of oxygen. Desulfuromonas is most prevalent in anaerobic marine and estuarine sediments. It can also be isolated from methane digesters and anaerobic hydrogen-sulfide rich mud of freshwater habitats. This genus consist of 5 species viz., D. acetoxidans , D. acetexigens , D. chloroethenica , D. palmitatis and D. thiophila .
gdesc.Bacteria|Desulfotomaculum: They are Gram-positive, straight or curved rods. They exhibit motility due to peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell) or polar flagella. Their growth usually takes place in the absence of oxygen. Since they are spore-forming bacteria they can even survive in dry and oxygen rich conditions. They are the predominant sulfate reducers collected during the flooded rice rhizosphere. Some of its important members are D. nigrificans, D. acetoxidans and D. thermoacetoxidans.This genus consist of 22 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Edwardsiella: Members of Edwardsiella are Gram-negative, motile, rod shaped bacteria. Edwardsiella can be isolated from human clinical specimens. The best described species is E.tarda , which has been infrequently isolated from warm blooded animals other than human, such as dogs, pigs, cattle, monkeys, rats etc. The most common manifestation of infection with E.tarda is gastrointestinal disease. It is commonly observed to be associated with Diarrhoea. We know only four species of Edwardsiella viz., E. tarda , E. ictaluri , E.hoshinae , and E.anguillimortifera .
gdesc.Bacteria|Enterobacter: They are gram-negative rod shaped bacteria. They exhibit motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They exhibit motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell). Enterobacter are found in the natural environment habitats such as water, sewage, vegetables and soil. Its members are now increasingly encountered as nosocomial infectious agents in urinary tract infections and bacteremia. Some of its important members are Enterobacter cloacae, Enterobacter cancerogenus and Enterobacter aerogenes . This genus comprises of 17 genera.
gdesc.Bacteria|Enterobcter: They are gram-negative rod shaped bacteria. They exhibit motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Enterobacter are found in the natural environment habitats such as water, sewage, vegetables and soil. Its members are now increasingly encountered as nosocomial infectious agents in urinary tract infections and bacteremia. Some of its important members are Enterobacter cloacae, Enterobacter cancerogenus and Enterobacter aerogenes . This genus comprises of 17 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Enterococcus: The members of this genus are Gram-positive cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria), which occur mostly in pairs or in short chains. Few species are pigmented (E. mundtii , E. casseliflavus) and non-motile but a few may be motile (E. casseliflavus, E. gallinarum) . They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Enteroccoci are predominantly inhabitants of the intestine of humans and other animals. E.faecium is the most frequently occurring enterococcal species in healthy chickens. In humans E. faecalis and E. faecium are the most frequent species and may cause intra-abdominal and pelvic infections. This genus comprise of 29 species. Some of its important members are E.faecalis , E. canis and E. sulfurous .
gdesc.Bacteria|Entrococcus: The members of this genus are Gram-positive cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria), which occur mostly in pairs or in short chains. Few species are pigmented (E. mundtii and E. casseliflavus) and non-motile but a few may be motile (E. casseliflavus and E. gallinarum) . They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Enteroccoci are predominantly inhabitants of the intestine of humans and other animals. E.faecium is the most frequently occurring enterococcal species in healthy chickens. In humans E. faecalis and E. faecium are the most frequent species and may cause intra-abdominal and pelvic infections. This genus comprise of 29 species. Some of its important members are E.faecalis , E. canis and E. sulfurous .
gdesc.Bacteria|Erwinia: The genus Erwinia comprise Gram-negative non-sporformoing , rod- shaped bacteria. They exhibit motility by peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Erwinia are generally pathogenic to plants, mainly potato. They have been reported from surface water, streams, rivers, lakes, reservoirs etc. one species Erwinia herbicola has been implicated as the causal agent for bacteremia, soft tissue infections, brain abscesses, septicimia and even meningitis. Erwinia amylovora , Erwinia dissolvens and Erwinia herbicola are some of its important members.
gdesc.Bacteria|Erysiphelothrix: Members of this genus are Gram-positive, non-sporeforming rods. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. It has been found as the common commensal or a pathogen in a wide variety of vertebrates and invertebrate species, including swine, sheep, cattle, horses, dogs, kangaroos, mice, house flies, ticks, mites, etc. In humans they occur as opportunistic pathogens. This genus comprises of only three species viz., E. rhusiopathiae , E.inopinata and E.tonsillarum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Escherichia: The Escherichia are Gram-negative (they do not retain crystal violet colour in Gram staining procedure and are therefore Gram-negative) rod shaped bacteria. They show motility by means of peritichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the cell). Normally they are found in aquatic environment and also in intestinal tracts of human beings and other animals. Mainly they are pathogenic to humans and may cause mild to severe gastroenteritis. The most famous member (species) of the genus is E.coli . Researchers to decipher many secrets of biological processes have extensively used this species. The genus consists of 7 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Flavobacterium: Strains of Flavobacteium are Gram-negative, non -motile, rod shaped bacteria. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. The members of this genius have been isolated from fresh and marine water, soil and ocean sediments, food- processing plants and clinical materials. They have been found to be pathogenic against humans in many cases Flavobacterium meningosepticum , the best-known pathogen in this genus, is associated with fatal meningitis of infants and has been isolated from their throat, spinal fluid and blood. Both F.multivorum and F. odoratum have been reported as a causative agent of bacterimia.This genus comprises of 52 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Flexibacter: Members of Flexibacter are Gram negative, long flexible thread like aerobic bacteria. Often colonies of these bacteria are colored yellow to orange because of caratenoid or flexirubin pigments. Flexibcter exhibit gliding motility by rapidly moving latex beads attached over their surface. The main habitats of the Flexibacter are soils at or close to neutral pH; decaying plant materials and dung of animals (particularly that of herbivores); in fresh water environments; on riverbanks and the lakeshores, in estuaries, aerobic bottom sediments and algal mats. In marine environments the Flexibacter are abundant near the shores; on living and dead seaweeds; in aerobic and anaerobic bottom sediments; and on decaying sea animals, such as crustaceans with their chitin exoskeleton. This genus consist of 17 species and some of its important members are F. flexilis , F .aggregans F. Canadensis and F. elegans .
gdesc.Bacteria|Flexithrix: Members of Flexithrix are Gram negative, long flexible thread like aerobic bacteria. Often colonies of these bacteria are coloured yellow to orange because of caratenoid or flexirubin pigments. Flexithrix exhibit gliding motility by rapidly moving latex beads attached over their surface. The main habitats of the Flexithrix are soils at or close to neutral pH, decaying plant materials, and dung of animals (particularly that of herbivores). In fresh water environments, they are found on riverbanks and the lakeshores, in estuaries, aerobic bottom sediments and algal mats. In marine environments the Flexithrix are abundant near the shores; on living and dead seaweeds; in aerobic and anaerobic bottom sediments and on decaying sea animals, such as crustaceans with their chitin exoskeleton. One distinguishing character of this genus from Flexibacter is that it can change its cell morphology in response to environmental conditions. The only known species in this genus is Flexithrix dorotheae .
gdesc.Bacteria|Frankia: The members of this genus are Gram-positive bacteria. They produce filamentous mycelium (a mass of branching hyphae-tubular filaments) that can differentiate into sporangia. Their optimum growth takes place under low level of oxygen concentration. They grow slow in laboratory conditions. They grow in symbiotic association often forming root nodule in at least eight families of higher non-leguminous plants (e.g., alder trees). They fix atmospheric nitrogen thus helps in nitrogen cycling. Only one species Frankia alni comprises this genus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Frateuria: Its members are Gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria. They exhibit motility due to polar flagellated cells. Their growth occurs only in the presence of oxygen. Only two habitat of Frateuria are known i.e., a plant Lilium auratum and the fruits of the Rubus parvifalius . This genus comprises of only one species F. aurantia.
gdesc.Bacteria|Fusobacterium: The genus Fusobacterium includes several species of Gram-negative rods, some are slender spindle shaped bacillus others are pleomorphic rods with parallel sides and rounded ends. They exhibit motility and grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. The normal habitat of Fusobacterium lies in the mouth, gastrointestinal tract and clinical samples of humans and animals. All Fusobacterium species are parasites of humans and animals. Pathogenic Fusobacterium are in particular isolated from inflammatory processes accompanied by necrosis and ulceration. They are most frequently found in head and neck infection, abscesses of the brain and the liver, and in infection following human and animal bites. This genus comprises of 24 genera. Some of its important members are F. nucleatum , F. necrophorum and F.perfoetens
gdesc.Bacteria|Gluconobacter: Gluconobacter strains are Gram-negative rods and exhibit motility by means of polar flagella. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. The habitat of Gluconobacter is relatively well known due to the considerable economic profits and losses that these bacteria cause in the industry. In nature these types of bacteria seems particularly well adopted to sugary and alcoholic solutions. They are also found in other niches such as flowers, fruits, beehives and palm wine. They are used in vinegar manufacture and their role, as spoilers of beer and wine, are well known. This genus consists of only four species viz., Gluconobacter oxydans, Gluconobacter cerinus , Gluconobacter frateurii and Gluconobacter asaii.
gdesc.Bacteria|Hafnia: The genus Hafnia is composed of Gram-negative rods. They exhibit motility by peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of bacterial cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. A member of this genus occurs in various clinical specimens and seems to be an opportunistic pathogen. Hafnia alvei, causative agent of intestinal disorders, have been isolated from sporadic causes of gastroenteritis. They are distributed in animals and birds and in natural environments such as soil, sewage and water. Only species known in this genus is Hafnia alvei.
gdesc.Bacteria|Halobacterium: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria. They show motility by means of polar flagella. Their growth occurs only in the presence of oxygen. Their natural habitats are the highly saline waters or soils of evaporatic systems. Such environment includes both naturally occurring saline lakes as well as artificial saline lagoons (e.g., solar saltern lagoons). This genus comprises of 13 species. Some important members of this genus are Halobacterium salinarum, Halobacterium saccharovorum, Halobacterium saccharovorum and Halobacterium halobium.
gdesc.Bacteria|Helicobacter: Helicobacter are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming, curved rod shaped bacteria.they are motile due to multiple sheathed flagella.These organisms grow better under microaerobic conditions (i.e., under less oxygen requirement). It is found in the gastric mucosa of humans and other animals.One of the important species of this genus H.pylori can cause peptic ulcer formation (lesions of the gastric mucosal membranes).This genus comprises of 23 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Herbaspirillum: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, generally vibroid , sometimes helical shaped bacteria. Herbaspirillum show very pronounced aerotactic movements by means of one to three bipolar flagella. They grow well under low level of oxygen concentration. Herbaspirillum occur in soil and are enriched on the root surfaces of many different plants like maize, sorghum and rice. This genus consist of only five species viz., H. seropedicae, H. rubrisubalbicans , H. lusitanum ,H. frisingense and H. chlorophenolicum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Hyphomicrobium: Hyphomicrobium cells stains Gram-negative and are rod shaped or ovoid to nearly spherical. They exhibit motility by means of more than one polar or sub polar flagella. They are chemoheterotrophs i.e., they are incapable of utilizing carbon dioxide as sole source of carbon and require one or more organic compounds for nutrition. Hyphomicrobium are found in nutrient rich freshwater habitat, brackish water and soil. Hyphomicrobium has got ecological role in the purification of water. This genus consist of 14 species and some of its important species are Hyphomicrobium neptunium , Hyphomicrobium coagulans and Hyphomicrobium denitrificans .
gdesc.Bacteria|Hyphomonas: Members of this genus are Gram-negative bacteria. They have a tendency to give rise to two dissimilar cells that are morphologically and behaviorally different after reproduction. Their optimum growth takes place in the presence of oxygen. Their habitat is generally confined to the deep-sea hydrothermal vents. This genus consists of 8 species. Some of its important members are Hyphomonas polymorpha , Hyphomonas adhaerens and Hyphomonas rosenbergii .
gdesc.Bacteria|Janthinobacterium: The members of this genus are Gram-negative rods with rounded ends, sometime slightly curved. They are usually motile by means of both a single polar flagellum and by one to four lateral flagella. They are strict aerobes. Members of Janthinobacterium have been isolated from water and soil, from river cracks lakes and springs. They are frequently isolated from a variety of floods i.e., processed poultry; various vegetables. They are sometime the cause of food spoilage. This genus comprises only two species viz., Janthinobacterium lividum and Janthinobacterium agaricidamnosum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Jonesia: Its members are Gram-positive, slender rods, mainly arranged singly; branched Y and club-like forms occur. Filaments and coccoid cells may be present in old cultures. They exhibit motility by peritrichous flagella at both 25 °C and 37 °C. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They have been isolated from the blood of ox blood, but their natural habitat is not known. This genus comprise of only one species i.e., Jonesia denitrificans (Type species).
gdesc.Bacteria|Klebsiella: klebsiella are straight Gram-negative rods, often surrounded by a capsule. They are non-motile. They are facultative anaerobes i.e., they may grow in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. klebsiella are found in a variety of environmental situations such as soil, vegetation, water, in human feces etc. Strains of klebsiella pneumioniae that are associated with plants (e.g., living or decaying wood and bark) differ from those associated with serious human infection pneumonia. Some of its important members are klebsiella pneumioniae , klebsiella mobilis and klebsiella granulomatis . This genus comprises of 12 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Kluyvera: The members of this genus are Gram-negative straight rods. They exhibit motility by scant peritrichous flagella. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They generally occur in food soil, sewage, and human clinical specimens, most often in respiratory tract and feces and occasionally in blood. Kluyvera species are infrequent opportunistic pathogens. This genus comprises of only four species viz., K. ascorbata , K. cochleae , K. cryocrescens and K. Georgiana .
gdesc.Bacteria|Kurthia: The members of this genus are Gram-positive, unbrancheed, rods with rounded ends in young cultures, and forms long chains. Older cultures are usually composed of coccoid cells. They exhibit motility by peritrichous flagella. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. Non-pathogenic Kurthia species are widely distributed in the environment and are common in animal feces and meat products. This genus comprises of only three species viz., Kurthia zopfii , Kurthia sibirica and Kurthia gibsonii .
gdesc.Bacteria|Lactobacillus: Lactobacillus are characterized as Gram-positive, non-sporeforming rods. They generally grow in the presence of oxygen but some are strict anaerobes.They can be found in soil, water, sewage, manure, plants and material of plants origin; also in the intestinal tract of various animals. They are generally the nonpathogenic bacteria which are useful to humans in several respects for ex. Lactobacillus lactis is used in the production of curd. The genus lactobacillus presently comprises of nearly 126 species. Some of its important species are lactobacillus acidophilus, lactobacillus lactis and lactobacillus piscicola .
gdesc.Bacteria|Lactococcus: Lactococcus cells are Gram – positive spherical or ovoid, occurring in pairs and short chains in liquid media. They lack motility and can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. A numbers of carbohydrates are fermented by lacttococcus with the production of lactic acid. They are found mainly in dairy and plant products.lactococci are employed in single and mixed cultures for the production of different kinds of cheese, fermented milk, cultured butter, and casein.this genus comprises of five species viz., L. lactis , L. garvieae, L. piscium, L. plantarum and L. raffinolactis .
gdesc.Bacteria|Leptospira: They are Gram-negative, thin-coiled helical shaped bacteria. leptospira are aerobic or microaerphilic (i.e., low level of oxygen is required for its optimal growth). They exhibit motility. leptospira are ubiquitous, associated with most mammals and with marsupials and certain amphibia or found free living in soil and surface water. Some strains of leptospira can cause an acute generalized infection characterized by fever and hemorrhages, called leptospirosis. This genus consist of 13 species and some of its important species are leptospira interrogans, leptospira biflexa and leptospira alexanderi.
gdesc.Bacteria|Leptospirillum: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, vibroid or spiral-shaped. They exhibit motility by means of a single polar flagellum. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen and acidic environment respectively. They are widely distributed in natural and industrial environments where the accelerated oxidation of sulfide ores create acidic, metal rich ecosystem. Some strains are moderately thermophile. Widely distributed in sulfide ore deposits where it might predominate over thiobacillus because of higher affinity to ferrous iron. This genus comprises of only three species viz., L.ferrooxidans , L. thermoferrooxidans and L. ferriphilum .
gdesc.Bacteria|Leuconostoc: Members of this genus are gram-positive, non-motile and non-sporeforming, short rods with rounded ends in long chain. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. They are found widely distributed in on plants and in dairy and other food products. Leuconostocs have increasingly been associated with the spoilage of meat and meat products. They may bring undesirable effect in fresh milk. They are non-pathogenic to plants and animals, but L.citreum and L. pseudomesentroidrs have been isolated from human sources. This genus comprises of 16 species and some of its important members are L. mesenteroides , L.lactis and L. citreum .
gdesc.Bacteria|Listeria: Its members are Gram-positive, non-sporeforming, short rods with rounded ends. Some times they are almost coccoid occurring singly or in short chains. They are motile by a few peritrichous flagella. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Members of this genus are widely distributed in the environment. In nature they can be found in soil, on rotting vegetation, in sewage and wastewater, in rivers and canals, and in salt estuaries. They can also be isolated from the feces of apparently healthy humans and animals. Some species are pathogenic for humans and animals for e.g., L. monocytogenes causes listeriosis in animals and humans. This genus comprises of 18 species and some of its important members are L. monocytogenes , L. denitrificans and L. seeligeri .
gdesc.Bacteria|Lyngbya: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, filamentous, photosynthetic bacteria. Their discs shaped cells are arranged in a chain (trichome) within an investing sheath. They produce a distinct, persistent and firm sheath. Trichomes are usually immotile within the sheath. Lyngbya has a worldwide distribution, species occurring in benthic marine and freshwater habitats. One easily identified species (L.aestuarii) form extensive mats in many in many intertidal mud flats and marshes. Lyngbya also occur extensively as attached elongate tufts in subtidal , protected marine waters.
gdesc.Bacteria|Macrococcus: Members of this genus are Gram-positive, non-motile cocci that usually forms irregular clusters. They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Their habitat lies in the cattles milk. No pathogenic capacity could be allotted to this bacterium seem seldom isolated. This genus comprises of 7 species and some of its members Macrococcus equipercicus, Macrococcus caseolyticus and Macrococcus lamae.
gdesc.Bacteria|Marinococcus: Cells of its members are spherical (occurring singly, in pairs or occasionally in tetrads) and Gram-positive. Often show motility by a few peritrichous flagella. They grow in the presence of oxygen. They are generally found in marine habitats and saline soils. This genus consists of four Marinococcus albus , Marinococcus hispanicus and Marinococcus halophilus .
gdesc.Bacteria|Marinomonas: Members of this genus are non-sporeforming. Gram-negative curved rods. They exhibit motility by means of single polar flagella. They grow well in the presence of oxygen. Their habitat lies in coastal waters and the open oceans; in highly varied biotopes; surfaces of biological or non- biological submerged material, seawater, sediment and gut of marine animals. This genus consists of four Marinomonas communis , Marinomonas primoryensis and Marinomonas vaga.
gdesc.Bacteria|Mastigocladus: They are gram-negative, photosynthetic filamentous bacteria. The true branches of this filamentous cynobacteria are uniseriate (arranged in a single row or series of cells that are generally longer than broad.  They are found commonly in neutral pH and alkaline hot springs throughout the world.
gdesc.Bacteria|Merismopedia: Unlike many cyanobacteria members of this genus are Gram-negative, unicellular strains those possesses spherical cells. Cells remain held together by slime material to form order colonies. Over 30 species of Merisopedia are found in freshwater and marine habitats, including bog communities and sand flats. They form rectangular colonies that may be free-floating or form thin films on the substrates.
gdesc.Bacteria|Mesorhizobium: Members of this genus are Gram-negative rods. They exhibit motility and grow in the presence of oxygen. They are soil and rhizosphere bacteria of agronomic importance because they perform nitrogen-fixing symbiosis with leguminous plants. This genus consist of eight species Mesorhizobium loti, Mesorhizobium mediterraneum and Mesorhizobium plurifarium .
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanobacterium: Members of this genus generally stain Gram-positive and have rod shape structure. Rods are long and form chains or often filaments. They lack motility and grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. Members of this genus may be found in Methanogenic environments such as anaerobic digestors, fresh water sediments, marshy soils, and the rumen of cattle or sheep. This genus consists of 22 species and some of its important members are Methanobacterium formicicum, Methanobacterium mobile and Methanobacterium ruminantium.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanobrevibacter: This genus includes Gram-positive bacteria and their shape varies from oval rods or cocci to short rods, usually occurring in pairs or chains. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen and are non-motile. Methanobrevibacter species occur in ruminant, human and other animal gastrointestinal tracts, termite hindgut, human oral cavity, municipal sewage sludge, decaying wood tissues and rice paddy soils. This genus consist 12 members and some of tis important members are Methanobrevibacter ruminantium, Methanobrevibacter wolinii and Methanobrevibacter oralis.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanococcoides: Its members are Gram-negative irregular cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacteria), occurring singly or in pairs. They lack motility and grow strictly in the absence of oxygen and high salt concentration. They are generally found in anaerobic marine sediments. The only known species in this genus is M.methylutens .
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanococcus: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, irregular cocci. They exhibit motility by means of polar tufts of flagella. Their growth occurs strictly in the absence of oxygen. They have a requirement foe higher concentration of NaCl for growth. This genus contains methane-producing cocci, which did not form regular packets (i.e., Methanosarcina ).
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanogenium: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, irregular cocci occurring singly or in pairs. No motility is observed although some strains flagellated. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. The cells occur in anaerobic marine or freshwater sediments, where they presumably function as hydrogen scavengers. This genus consist of twelve species and some of its important members are , and Methanogenium thermophilicum .
gdesc.Bacteria|methanohalobium: Its members are Gram-negative, irregular cocci (cells are flat, polygonal, or irregular spherical bodies). They lack motility and grow strictly in the absence of oxygen and high salt concentration (extremely halophilic). Members of this genus are generally found in anaerobic marine sediments. This genus consist of only one species i.e., Methanohalobium evestigatum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanohalophilus: Its members are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming and extremely irregular cocci. They lack motility and grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. They are moderate halophiles i.e., they grow at moderate concentration of salt. They may be found in natural or artificial saline lakes or saline ground water. This genus consist of five species and some of its important members are Methanohalophilus mahii, Methanohalophilus oregonensis and Methanohalophilus zhilinae.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanolobus: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming, irregular cocci. They exhibit motility by means of monotrichous flagella (bacteria with only one flagella). They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen and low concentration of salt. Methanolobus is commonly found in anaerobic sea sediments with in situ temperature between 10-45°C and pH value between 5-8. M.oregonensis has been found in alkaline aquifers.this genus consist of six species only and some of its important members are Methanolobus tindarius, Methanolobus vulcani and Methanolobus bombayensis .
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanomicrobium: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming, short curved rods. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. Its members may be motile by means of monotrichous polar flagellum. Methanomicrobium has been isolated from bovine rumen. Only species known to this genus is M.mobile. This genus consist of only two species viz., Methanomicrobium mobile and Methanomicrobium paynteri .
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanoplanus: Its members are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming irregular cocci or plate shaped. They occur singly or in pairs and are sometimes branched without septa. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. Methanoplanus has been isolated from an anaerobic environment with a swamp, from an oil producing well, and from a marine saprophytic ciliate. This genus consist of only three species viz., Methanoplanus limicola , Methanoplanus petrolearius and Methanoplanus endosymbiosus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanosarcina: Members of this genus are, non-sporeforming, non-motile, irregular spheroid bodies; occurring alone or in aggregates of cells. They show variable Gram-stain results. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen and are slightly acidophilic (i.e., these bacteria can grow at a low pH also). Members of this genus may be isolated from freshwater and marine environments, where acetate or methylamines are degraded. These include anaerobic digestors, fresh water and marine sediments and the rumen of cattle and sheep.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanospirillum: Methanospirillum are rod shaped,Gram-negative bacteria.they have a distinctive spiral morphology. Methanospirillum cells may form long chains or filaments, encased by a continous sheath or be single.since this genus falls under the Methanogenic Bacteria, they are the major source ofd atmospheric nitrogen,common habitat for this genus are anaerobic digestors,flooded soils and gastrointestinal tracts. Methanospirillum hungatei and Methanospirillum hungatii are the only known Methanospirillum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanothermobacter: Species of this genus are Gram-positive, non-motile, curved or crooked slender rods. Cells produce fimbriae (filamentous appendages). Members of this genus have been isolated from thermophilic, anaerobic, sewage sludge digestors and river sediment.this genus consist of six species and some of its important members are Methanothermobacter thermautotrophicus, Methanothermobacter thermoflexus and Methanothermobacter wolfei.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methanothrix: Its members are Gram-negative, non-sporeforming, non-motile large sheathed rods. They grow strictly in the absence of oxygen. They can be isolated from mesophilic and theromophilic anaerobic digestors treating domestic wastes; from granular sludge, anaerobic fixed –bed reactors and other types of anaerobic systems. This genus consist of 5 species and some of its important members are Methanothrix soehngenii , Methanothrix thermoacetophila and Methanothrix thermophila.
gdesc.Bacteria|Methylobacterium: They are Gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria, occurring singly or occasionally in rosettes. They show motility by single polar, sub polar, or lateral flagella, although some strains are vigorously motile. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. Members of the genus have been isolated from soil, dust, fresh water, lake sediments, leaf surfaces and nodules, rice grains, air, and hospital environments.this genus consist of 14 species and some of its important members are Methylobacterium organophilum, Methylobacterium radiotolerans and Methylobacterium rhodinum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Microbacterium: Members of the genus are Gram-positive, slender, irregular rods in young cultures; arranged singly or in pairs, when some are arranged at an angle to give V formation. They grow in the presence of oxygen. Their habitat lies in dairy products, sewage and insects. This genus consist of 35 genus and some of its important members are Microbacterium aerolatum, Microbacterium dextranolyticum and Microbacterium halophilum.
gdesc.Bacteria|Microbispora: They are Gram-positive, filamentous bacteria. A stable branched mycelium (a mass of branching tubular filaments) carries spores in characteristic longitudinal airs on aerial mycelium; spores are not usually formed on the substrate mycelium. They grow in the presence of oxygen. Spores are non-motile and their surface is smooth. Generally they are located in soil.
gdesc.Bacteria|Micrococcus: Its members are Gram-positive with spherical cells, occurring in pairs, tetrads or irregular clusters, not in chains they seldom show motility. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. They occur primarily on mammalian skin and in soil but commonly are isolated from food products and the air
gdesc.Bacteria|Microcoleus: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, filamentous, photosynthetic bacteria. Members of this genus have two to several trichomes (a chain of cells without an investing sheath) oriented parallel, which are often spirally and tightly interwoven, and enclosed by a common homogenous sheath. Cells composing the trichomes are longer than wide mature end cells are conical. They exhibit slow gliding motility. Members of the genus have been an important component of intertidal mats, including mats of hyper saline waters.
gdesc.Bacteria|Microcystis: Members of this genus are Gram-negative photosynthetic bacteria. Cells are oval to spherical. May be united into colonial aggregates by mucilage, but are never enclosed by multi laminated sheath material. Gas vesicles are normally present. They have planktonic habitat i.e., free floating, mostly microscopic microorganisms that can be found in almost all waters. â-cyclocitral is also released by Microcystis , and is one of the odor contributing compounds of old Microcystis blooms in lakes and ponds.
gdesc.Bacteria|Micropolyspora: They are Gram-positive filamentous bacteria with well-developed, branched, septate mycelium (a mass of branching tubular filaments). Non-motile spores are borne singly, sessile, or on short and long sporophore, that often occurs in branched clusters. Generally they grow in the presence of oxygen. They are the common inhabitants of soil, water, marine environments and sediments. A few strains, anaerobic and of uncertain taxonomy have been reported in the intestinal tract of termite and rumen of sheep. Micromonospra actively degrades chitin and cellulose and it can produce antibiotics such as gentamicin.this genus consist of 23 species. And some of its important members are Micromonospora chalcea , Micromonospora halophytica and Micromonospora pallida.
gdesc.Bacteria|Microtetraspora: They are Gram-positive filamentous bacteria with stable extensively branched vegetative mycelium. Aerial mycelia bear pairs or short chains of spores. Their growth take pace in the presence of air. They are widely distributed in soil. This genus consist of 21 genus and some of its important members are Microtetraspora glauca, Microtetraspora viridis and Microtetraspora fastidiosa.
gdesc.Bacteria|Moraxella: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, rods. The rods are often very short and plump, frequently approaching a coccus shape. Generally they grow in the presence of oxygen, but some strains may grow weakly under anaerobic conditions. Flagella are absent. Swimming motility is absent, but surface bound twitching motility has been observed in some rod-shaped species. With the exception of M. (M.) bovis , all species of the Moraxella subgenus are found as a parasite in association with mucosal surface of humans and other warm-blooded animals. This genus comprises of 6 species and some of its important members are Moraxella (Moraxella) lacunata, Moraxella (Moraxella) bovis and Moraxella (Moraxella) atlantae
gdesc.Bacteria|Morganella: Members of this genus are Gram-negative Straight rods. They show motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the cell). They can grow both in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Morgnellla occur in feces of humans, dogs, other mammals, and reptiles. They are opportunistic secondary invaders, isolated from bacteremia, respiratory tract wound and urinary tract infections. This genus consists of only one species Morganella morganii.
gdesc.Bacteria|Mycobacterium: Mycobacterium members are acid- fast actinomycetes (filamentous bacteria). They are slightly curved or straight non-motile rods. The members of Mycobacterium may be aerobic or microaerophilic (they require low level of oxygen for growth). Mycobacterium species have been isolated from a diverse environment of fresh and salt water, soil, and dust. Some of its members are also found in household pets such as goats, dogs and birds. They may be obligate parasites, opportunistic pathogens, or free living saprophytes (organisms that usually grow on decomposing organic matter). Mycobacterium tuberculosis, causative agent of tuberculosis and Mycobacterium leprae, which causes leprosy in human beings are two important pathogenic members of this genus. This genus comprises of 121 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Mycoplasma: Mycoplasmas are the smallest bacterial cells that can reproduce independently. Since they lack cell wall, they stains Gram-negative. Mycoplasmas vary in shape from pear shaped structures to branched or helical filaments. They are non-motile and have no flagella. However some human pathogens like Mycoplasma pneumoniae exhibit gliding motility on liquid covered surface. Mycoplasmas are facultative anaerobes i.e., they can grow in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Growth of some species such as Mycoplasma mycoides and Mycoplasma pneumoniae appear to be improved by aeration. The mycoplasmas are parasites of humans, arthropods and plants. The primary habitats of human and animal mycoplasmas are the mucous surfaces of the respiratory and urogenital tracts, eyes, alimentary canal, mammary glands and joints in some animals. Some of the disease causing mycoplasmas are M.pneumoniae , causative agent of typical pneumonia; M.fermentans which causes human respiratory and joint diseases. This genus comprises of 121 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Myxococcus: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, unicellular, gliding bacteria with rod shaped vegetative cells. They have a complex life cycle withy the production of fruiting bodies, and the formation of dormant myxospores that frequently are enclosed in walled structures called sporengioles or sporangia. They grow strictly in the presence of oxygen. Most Myxococcus are micro-predators or scavengers. They secrete an array of digestive enzymes that lyses bacteria, yeast and certain filamentous fungi. They are most commonly isolated from neutral soils or decaying plant materials such as leaves and tree bark and from animal dung. This genus comprises of 8 species and some of its important members are Myxococcus fulvus, Myxococcus macrosporus and Myxococcus xanthus .
gdesc.Bacteria|Myxosarcina: Members of this genus are Gram-negative, unicellular rods or cocci. They form irregular to nearly true cubical aggregates by Binary fission. Usually each wall of aggregates form four small motile baeocyte by internal multiple fission. Few strains of Myxosarcina have been observed to exhibit gliding motility. Strains of Myxosarcina have been isolated from snail shell collected in intertidal zone requiring elevated salt concentration typical of marine forms.
gdesc.Bacteria|Neisseria: The genus Neisseria is a representative example of Gram-negative bacteria, which forms relatively large cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacterial cells) that looks like kidney beans. Neisseria may grow in the presence as well as in the absence of oxygen. Nisseria habitat lies in humans as well as in other animals. All species can colonize the oro- and nasopharynx. The throats of animals are also the habitat for Neisseria. The members of Neisseria are generally the human pathogens. Neisseria gonorrhaeae and Neisseria meningitidis are some important human pathogens. This genus comprises of 24 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Nitrosomonas: Nitrosomonas are Gram-negative, short rods. Its cells are ellipsoidal; occur singly in pairs or in short chains. They are aerobic in nature i.e., requires oxygen for its growth. They exhibit motility by means of polar flagella. They generally are ubiquitous in soil, fresh water and marine environment. However many species have been observed to occur predominantly or exclusively in special sites such as sewage disposal system, brackish waters or oceans. These bacteria are of considerable ecological significance since they help in oxygen recycling. There are 9 species in this genus. Some important members of this genus are Nitrosomonas europaea,Nitrosomonas halophila and Nitrosomonas cryoloterans
gdesc.Bacteria|Pseudomonas: Pseudomonas are Gram-negative, straight or curved rods. They exhibit motility by means of polar flagella. Members of this genus are aerobic i.e., oxygen is required for their growth. Pseudomonas are widespread in nature and particularly abundant in soil and water, but some are also colonizer and pathogens of plants and animals. Some species are medically important and can be isolated from clinical samples. Pseudomonas aerogenosa is an opputunistic pathogen which can be isolated from wound burn& urinary tract infections. Some other human pathogens are Pseudomonas malleli and Pseudomonas pseudomalleli . There are 164 species of Pseudomonas, that has been described.
gdesc.Bacteria|Salmonella: Salmonella are Gram-negative, rod -shape bacteria. They show motility by means of peritrichous flagella (flagella present all around the body of the cell). The principal habitat of Salmonella is the intestinal tracts of humans and animals. Salmonella are disseminated in the natural environment (water, soil, sometimes plants used as food) through human or animal excretion. Some of the major human pathogens from this genera are Salmonella enteritidis, causative agent of Salmonellosis; Salmonella typhi , causative agent of typhoid fever. Salmonella comprises of 12 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Sphaerotilus: They stains Gram-negatively. Sphareotilus cells occurs within a filamentous structure known as sheath. This sheath confers protection against the predators and parasites. They are arranged in one single chain, rarely in two or three rows and show motility due to the presence of polar flagella. Sphareotilus grows strictly in the presence of oxygen. Its normal habitat lies in fresh water heavily contaminated with sewage or wastewater from paper dairy and other agricultural industries. The only known species of Sphareotilus is S.natans.
gdesc.Bacteria|Spirillum: Members of the genus Spirillum are Gram-negative. Their shape is like long rods twisted into spirals or helices. They are motile by means of lophotrichous flagella (i.e., a cluster of flagella at one or both ends of the cell). They require low level of oxygen for its growth, but are damaged by normal atmospheric oxygen level. Spirillum is widely distributed in many stagnant freshwater environments. S.volutans is the only known species of this genus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Staphylococcus: Staphylococci are Gram-positive, cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacterial cells) that forms grape like clusters. They are facultative anaerobes i.e., they do not require oxygen for growth but do grow better in its presence.Species of Staphylococcus commonly occur on skin surface of animals and human beings where they live without causing any disease. One of the well-known species of this genus - S.aureus, however, is a potential human pathogen, infecting wounds membranes, and lining and also causing food poisoning. It also causes boils of the skin.Other important species are S.epidermis and S.chromogenes.Altogether there are 52 species under this genus.
gdesc.Bacteria|Streptococcus: Streptococci are Gram-positive bacteria and the cells are cocci (roughly spherical shaped bacterial cells), which occur in chains or pairs. They are facultative anaerobes i.e., they do not require oxygen for growth but do grow better in its presence. Streptococci comprises a significant proportion of the normal microbial flora of the mouth, skin and mucous membranes of the respiratory, alimentary and urogenital tracts. They are important human pathogens. Oral streptococci are the main cause of dental carries, which cause tooth decay. One of the important human pathogen is Streptococcus pyogens ,causative agent of rheumatic fever. Some important streptococci are Streptoccocus facelis , S.boris and S.entricus.This genus comprises of 90 species.
gdesc.Bacteria|Vibrio: The members of this genus are Gram-negative, rod shaped bacteria that are curved to form a comma shape or an incomplete spiral.They show motility by mens of a single polar flagellum.They are capable of growing in the presence as well in the absence of oxygen.The species of Vibrio are widely distributed in marine as well as in the other aquatic environment and few species infect marine animals.Some Vibrio species causes intestinal human infections such as diarrhea and cholera.Its important members are Vibrio cholrae and Vibrio aerogenes.This genus comprises of 70 species.
